transcript: I think this may be one of my favourite directed pieces that I've seen all year. And there's a lot to love about the direction of this piece, from the giant chalkboard that serves as the backdrop that the cast will draw on and utilize throughout the show, to this production having its very own Sunset Boulevard moment. But the thing that I really wanna talk about is the way that this production builds a sense of community, not just with the people on stage, but with everyone in that theatre. And this is set up even before the play begins with as the audience is coming in and taking their seats, we also see the actors strolling into the theatre, having casual conversations before ultimately taking their seats on stage. It immediately tears down any barrier between the actors and the audience, and I think that this pays a lot of dividends as the show goes on. I also think that this sense of community is enhanced by the fact that Classic Stage Company is such an intimate theater. It really is one of those theaters where truly, wherever you are sitting, you are going to have a great view and you are going to feel connected to the action. So all of this serves to build up a sense of community, unity, only to have it ripped away from you. Because if you don't know, this is a show about a community that turns in on itself and This is where I issue a trigger warning, because this show can be really difficult to watch at times. It tells the true story of a group of classmates, half Jewish and half Catholic, living in Poland during World War 2 and everything that LED up to it. And given that description, you can probably guess that it does not end great for a lot of the Jews in this story. the real tragedy is that their fate was not sealed by German soldiers, but rather their friends and neighbors in the community. And it's that betrayal of community that feels so raw as an audience member, because the show did so much work to pull you in and make you feel like you are part of that community. And don't get me wrong, it. This play can be really difficult to watch at times, especially the end of Act 1, which is when the actual event happens. So if you are someone that does not like depictions of SA or mass unaliving, particularly of children and babies, I would say maybe stay away from this piece. But otherwise, I think that this is a really important piece of theater, and I hope that people go out and see it. It is harrowing and powerful, and I really have not stopped thinking about it since I saw it, which I think is a hallmark of a really good piece of theater. So if you are in New York between now and November 3rd. I definitely recommend checking this out at Classic Stage Company off Broadway.
